text:
Maya R: Hey team, seeing weird early-stop in streaming after HF->Redwood conversion + int8 quant. Model generates a handful of tokens then stream closes with EOS even though prompt expects long output.
Samir K: repro? config or tokenizer change during conversion?
Maya R: Minimal repro attached below. Happens only on quantized snapshot and only when streaming. Non-streamed generate is fine.
Maya R: ```python
# conversion call
convert_hf_to_redwood.py --model gpt-j-like --quantize 8 --save ./bundles/gptj-int8
# runtime call
client.stream_generate(model='gptj-int8', prompt=prompt, max_new_tokens=200)
```
Oliver P: can you paste config.json and tokenizer.special_tokens_map in the bundle? quick check for eos/bos mismatches.
Maya R: snippet from bundle/config.json:```json
{"eos_token_id": null, "bos_token_id": 1, "pad_token_id": 0, "vocab_size": 50257}
```
Maya R: tokenizer special tokens:```json
{"eos_token": "</s>", "bos_token": "<s>", "unk_token": "<unk>"}
```
Samir K: aha eos_token_id null could be the problem. HF tokenizer has token string but model config missing mapping to id. When streaming we check eos id to stop; null => fallback heuristics may stop early on byte pattern or second eos.
Maya R: interesting — but why only after quantization? the float32 bundle had eos_id set.
Oliver P: conversion script might reindex or trim tokenizer merges when applying quantization pipeline. I saw a bug where we rebuild tokenizer vocab for int8 to drop rare tokens, and forgot to recompute special token ids.
Nina S: Can you reproduce with --no-rebuild-tokenizer? maybe workaround is to force set eos_token_id in config.json to tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("</s>").
Maya R: tried patching config.json locally to "eos_token_id": 50256 and streaming worked (no early stop)
Dev Deploy Bot: uploaded bundle gptj-int8-fix1 to staging (id: bndl-7a9)
Maya R: logs from streaming worker showing token ids when it cut off:```
[2026-03-19T15:03:12Z] tokens: [102, 2456, 50256]
[2026-03-19T15:03:12Z] stream closed (reason: eos_token)
```
Maya R: then with patched config:```
[2026-03-19T15:10:04Z] tokens: [102, 2456, 2456, 78, 90,...]
[2026-03-19T15:11:00Z] stream closed (reason: max_new_tokens)
```
Samir K: That matches theory. Also saw cases where tokenizer emits multiple eos ids in a row (consecutive eos), our streaming code treats first as stop and closes. But some generation strategies (sampling temperature>1) produce repeated eos sub-tokens from byte-level tokenizers. We should consider: 1) respect eos_id once only if it is final by looking at logprobs? 2) require two consecutive eos? 3) configurable stop behavior.
Oliver P: For HF chat templates, some models embed stop sequences like "\n### End" in system prompt. Conversion currently moves these into chat_templates.stop but doesn't always set stop_token_ids. If both stop strings and eos id are present we sometimes get double-stop. Edge-case: user stop seq and eos both present => early abort when eos appears inside multi-token stop string.
Maya R: example where stop string contains eos token bytes (weird): tokenizer.encode("\n### End</s>") -> [198, 345, 50256] so stop string itself contains eos id. Our streaming stops at that eos even though intended stop is full string.
Nina S: For now workaround: in conversion, prefer explicit stop_token_ids list and remove bare eos mapping when stop strings present. Also add a flag stream_stop_strategy: ["string-first", "id-first", "both"]. Default "string-first".
Samir K: Also quantization path reorders KV cache layout; check that early close isn't from cache corruption triggering generation failure. But your logs show 'stream closed (reason: eos_token)' so it's not a crash.
Oliver P: Proposed short patch: in serving/runtime/streaming.py change on_token_emitted: if token_id == eos_id and pending_stop_buffer not empty -> buffer until we can match stop strings or until N tokens consumed. Then emit close. 
Maya R: Sounds good. We also need CI test: convert a HF model with a stop string that contains eos bytes, quantize int8, run streaming for 200 tokens, assert not closed before 190 tokens.
Nina S: I'll add a unit test in eng-ml/test_models/test_stream_eos_handling.py and a model fixture that encodes stop string to include eos.
Dev Deploy Bot: canary deploy of runtime patch to staging at 15:40 UTC
Maya R: thanks — assigning followups: @Samir K update conversion script to retain special token ids; @Oliver P runtime buffering patch; @Nina S tests + regression harness; I'll validate bundles on staging and report.
Samir K: quick note: also check config.json's "tie_word_embeddings" path; conversion used a different tokenizer version leading to off-by-one id shift.
Maya R: got it. will log all bundle diffs in the onboarding sheet.
Oliver P: FYI adding a small telemetry: when stream closes we will log the last 8 token ids and whether they match any configured stop strings — should help debug future cases.
Maya R: OK closing the loop once staging tests green. :thumbsup:
